$comment: Known differences from the TypeScript (mppx) reference adapter that scripts/diff_fuzz.py accepts. category: harmless (allowed by the protocol), sdk-bug (an SDK is wrong; remove the entry when it is fixed) or adapter-bug (a conformance adapter is wrong). An entry matches a divergence when its adapters (or *), operations and kinds match, every differing field is listed in fields, messagePattern matches the failing side's error message, and inputPattern matches the header, text or JSON input.

entries.reason: These adapters route operations through their legacy command path, which trims stdin (Python str.strip, Go strings.TrimSpace, Rust trim) before calling the SDK. The TypeScript adapter passes the input unchanged.
These adapters return a parsed opaque as the SDK's decoded map instead of its wire string, so the value fails the Challenge schema. No vector parses an opaque yet.
The Python adapter's format-www-authenticate and format-authorization build the Challenge without opaque, so the header loses it.
pympp, mpp-go and mpp-rs leave description out of a credential's challenge echo, so parsing or formatting a credential drops it. The challenge id does not bind description.

pympp 0.16 applies its header-safety check (no control characters or CR/LF) to every string in a credential's challenge echo, including description, and rejects the credential. mppx accepts them. The pinned pympp 0.11 does not check, so this only shows against pympp main.
The Rust adapter wraps a wire opaque string as {"_raw": ...} before formatting, so the header carries a different opaque.

pympp (1*LOWERALPHA) and mpp-go reject method ids with digits, ':', '_' or '-' after the first letter, which mppx and mpp-rs accept. vectors/www-authenticate.json extended_method_identifier is scoped to typescript and rust for the same reason.
pympp and mpp-go treat realm="" as missing. mppx and mpp-rs accept an empty realm, and the Challenge schema allows one.
mpp-go drops an empty challenge realm from a parsed credential, so the adapter's value fails the Credential schema.

mppx finds the Payment challenge in a WWW-Authenticate value that lists several challenges (RFC 9110 §11.6.1). pympp, mpp-go and mpp-rs parse only a value that is a single Payment challenge: another scheme before it is rejected, and one after it is read as more Payment parameters.
pympp, mpp-go and mpp-rs require a space after 'Payment'; mppx also accepts a tab. RFC 9110 separates the scheme with 1*SP.
mpp-rs mishandles whitespace around '=' in an auth-param (request = "e30"), which RFC 9110 allows as BWS and mppx accepts: it rejects the challenge or reads an empty value.
pympp accepts auth-params separated only by whitespace (id="a" realm="b"); RFC 9110 requires commas and mppx rejects them.

entries.messagePattern: at request: .* is not of type 'object'
entries.reason: mpp-rs accepts a challenge whose request decodes to a JSON array or scalar, so the adapter's value fails the Challenge schema. mppx rejects a request that is not an object.
pympp does not type-check a credential's optional challenge fields: "expires": true parses and is stringified to "True". mppx rejects it.
mpp-go and mpp-rs accept an Authorization value with text after the base64url credential (such as ', Basic realm="x"'); mppx rejects it.

pympp decodes credentials with base64.urlsafe_b64decode, which discards characters outside the alphabet, so a credential token with quotes, commas, '+', '/' or trailing text decodes where mppx rejects it.
pympp decodes receipts with base64.urlsafe_b64decode, which discards characters outside the alphabet, so a receipt with quotes, commas, '+', '/' or inner spaces decodes where mppx rejects it.
mpp-go and mpp-rs model a credential's source as a string (the payer DID): they reject an object source, or mpp-rs drops it when formatting. mppx and the Credential schema also allow an object.
pympp's parse_authorization sets source=str(data["source"]), so an object source becomes its Python repr ("{'amount': None}") instead of being kept or rejected.
mpp-rs canonicalizes the request with U+007F to U+009F escaped, while JCS (RFC 8785) escapes only U+0000 to U+001F, so ids for requests containing them differ from mppx's.
mpp-rs canonicalizes integral floats such as 0.0 as written, while JCS (RFC 8785) uses ECMAScript number serialization (0.0 becomes 0), so the ids differ from mppx's.

pympp's parse_www_authenticate is quadratic in the header length: 12 KB takes about 2 s, 48 KB about 26 s and 97 KB about 100 s, past the fuzzer's timeout. mppx, mpp-go and mpp-rs answer in milliseconds; mpp-go also caps the header size.
mpp-go rejects WWW-Authenticate and Authorization values above its size limit; mppx has none.
mpp-go refuses to bind a realm, method or intent containing '|', the HMAC input delimiter, so two challenges cannot share an id. mppx binds it as is.

pympp and mpp-go refuse to bind a credential header that is not an HTTP field name (an RFC 9110 token), such as one with quotes or ':'. mppx binds any string. A challenge cannot name such a header, so rejecting it is stricter, not wrong.
mppx's Credential.deserialize accepts a credential with no payload, so the reference value fails the Credential schema. The other SDKs reject it.
pympp and mpp-go re-render receipt timestamps, dropping zero milliseconds (2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z becomes 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z). Both name the same instant.
mppx's Receipt.serialize requires method and status "success"; the Receipt schema and other SDKs allow any status and no method.
mppx rejects a receipt whose optional string fields (such as externalId) are null; the other SDKs read null as absent.
mppx decodes non-canonical base64url (padding, a lone trailing character, non-zero trailing bits) that the other SDKs reject. Rejecting them is stricter, not wrong.
